title: Air-drying of cells enables visualization of antiparallel microtubule overlaps in the spindle midzone
author: Ifuji, Kuga, et al.

steps.title: Prepare drying apparatus
steps.instruction: Assemble the equipment: attach two pieces of double‑sided tape to an expanded polystyrene board to hold two culture dishes, and fix a hair dryer in a stand positioned approximately 7.5 cm above the board; adjust the dryer height according to the airflow strength.

steps.title: Remove culture medium
steps.instruction: Almost completely aspirate the culture medium from the cells on the cover slip using suction.

steps.title: Secure dish on tape
steps.instruction: Place the culture dish onto the double‑sided tape on the board so it cannot be displaced by the airflow.

steps.title: Air‑dry cells
steps.instruction: Blow cold air from the hair dryer onto the cells for 5 min; cells should appear dried. Adjust drying time if needed based on airflow strength and distance.

steps.title: Fix cells with PTEMF
steps.instruction: Fix the air‑dried cells with pre‑warmed PTEMF buffer (2 mM PIPES pH 6.8, 0.2 % Triton X‑100, 10 mM EGTA, 1 mM MgCl₂, 4 % formaldehyde) for 20 min on a water bath set to 30 °C. Place a metal tray on the water bath, add a small amount of water to the tray, and put the culture dishes on the tray to ensure efficient heat transfer.

steps.title: Wash and stain
steps.instruction: Wash the fixed cells with PBS(−). Permeabilize in PBS(−) containing 0.1 % saponin and 3 % bovine serum albumin, then incubate with the primary anti‑tubulin antibody for 1 h, wash, and incubate with the secondary antibody for 1 h following the standard immunofluorescence protocol.
